contract.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
contract.purpose: Select candidate warehouse instructions; cart regrouping can also persist sequence changes.
inputs_defaults: Thirteen declared inputs: workUnit nvarchar(50), containerId nvarchar(25), user nvarchar(30), workprofile nvarchar(25), workprofileSequence numeric(5), warehouse nvarchar(25), fromto int, fromLoc nvarchar(25), isSystemDirectedWork bit=0, isCartPickingWork bit=0, groupNumber int, transportContId nvarchar(25), isCcWorkUnit bit=0. Only the three bit flags have declared defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: Several strings use ISNULL-to-empty for branch choice; group checks use both numeric comparisons and ISNULL-to-empty. The table GROUP_NUM is nvarchar(50) while this input is int, so conversion behavior matters.
Missing configuration can leave variables NULL and make comparisons unknown or string concatenation NULL. No complete input-validation contract is enforced here.

The profile-wide SELECT has no sequence predicate or ordering, so multiple detail rows can assign differing values without a deterministic chosen row. The sequence-qualified SELECTs have a narrower scope.

Regroup ORDER_BY/TABLE_FIELD_NAME values become SQL syntax, not bound data parameters. The local regroup table is populated in sequence order, but TOP 1 reads from it have no ORDER BY; do not promise that the configured order is preserved.
output_shape: The final dynamic SELECT returns a branch-dependent instruction projection: instruction/work-unit/item/company identities; quantities/units; source, destination and pick/drop locations/warehouses; grouping/sequence; container, lot, serial/catch-weight and location verification metadata. System-directed branches add assignment, condition, priority and aging fields.
Row numbering is ROW_NUMBER or DISTINCT plus DENSE_RANK over a constant, depending on the feature branch. Numbering does not itself establish the final business ordering.

The top-limited performance branch combines a limited cycle-count key selection and non-cycle-count work with UNION ALL, then applies an outer TOP and order. It is not an unlimited list of every eligible task.

ordered_branches.explanation: If cart picking and not cycle-count work, infer group and sequence from matching transport containers; TOP 1 has no ORDER BY. If sequence is nonpositive and no already-picked detail has zero FROM_QTY, construct sort expressions from WORK_REGROUP_ORDER and dynamically assign ROW_NUMBER values to detail instructions in the group.

Otherwise choose a supplied positive group, or a neutral group condition. If work unit and both container inputs are absent, the non-system-directed initiation predicate is false and location initiation is marked; otherwise match work unit or transport container.

Compare the configured profile zones with the relevant ZONE subset. Read profile-wide grouping/initiation/to-assignment/multiple-unit values separately from sequence-qualified work types and from-assignment/container behavior; read delimiter settings and user authorization.

Build initial pick/putaway order; location initiation or system-directed picking can replace it with assignment-method order. A feature branch adds instruction ID as a tie breaker; another changes priority ordering to favor the specified user within priority.

Read the configurable top-row cap with TRY_CAST. Missing, nonnumeric or nonpositive cap becomes 2000. Determine source/destination quantity predicate and warehouse authorization branches from fromto and work-process context. Values other than 0, 1 or 2 have no documented validation branch.

Prepare zone, company, work-type, container, hold, condition, catch-weight and assignment predicates. For the gated system-directed location path, probe minimum priority and user assignment when applicable; then choose exact location, greater location or lower location in that order.

Create the local work-type table by splitting the configured work types. Build one of non-system-directed, system-directed performance/top-limited, performance/non-top, or legacy system-directed SELECTs; project branch-specific location/container metadata.
Execute the final SQL through sp_executesql with separately bound work unit, work types, user, warehouse, profile, container, source location, group and transport container parameters.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: The cart regroup branch writes WORK_INSTRUCTION.SEQUENCE. Candidate SELECTs do not themselves decrement inventory or complete work. No current work record was read.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: WORK_PROFILE_DETAIL, profile plus supplied sequence, work-profile zones, user/company/warehouse access and feature function results affect selection. Effective settings were not fetched.

Feature gates select complete SQL paths; they are not proven enabled by function existence. The row-cap fallback is 2000, not an observed configuration value. No universal sort order follows from AIM examples.
The variable receiptSequenceOrder is assigned but is not subsequently referenced in the captured body; no behavioral effect is attributed to it.
error_and_return_handling: No TRY/CATCH, explicit RAISERROR/THROW, dedicated status return or own rollback is present. Dynamic compilation, invalid configured identifiers, scalar-subquery cardinality and conversion errors can propagate. No execution was attempted.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: The group inference, picked-work check, resequencing and final selection are separate statements without a body-owned transaction or explicit reservation lock. Static selection is not proof of exclusive assignment or race-free execution.

Ordering can have ties in branches without the instruction-ID tie breaker; joining descriptive/location/container data can affect row cardinality. No runtime equivalence of performance and legacy branches is claimed.
contract.trigger_behavior: The observed WORK_INSTRUCTION trigger is AFTER INSERT; the selector performs UPDATE for regrouping, so that trigger is not directly activated by this operation.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Application caller, permission enforcement, claim/reservation, picking confirmation and caller transaction are not captured by this body.
Feature names and configuration values were not exposed. Full business-code enumeration and branch-equivalence validation remain separate review work.
Private SQL inspection establishes fixed base-table targets and SQL structure; arbitrary configured sort expressions prevent treating every possible generated statement as validated.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
Owner backup/leftover and item-master-failure suggestions are hypotheses. Name patterns and missing references do not validate them. No deletion recommendation is made.
Current replica status is owner-attested. This task documents the captured source as-is and requires no application version/build or extension development.
All claims are snapshot-scoped static evidence or explicitly labeled vendor behavior. No database/application operational execution.
A full body review with gaps is not whole-process semantic closure or runtime acceptance.
Code-family names never establish vendor/custom ownership.
